Maintainer ruling (2026-08-25, batch adjudication close-out; verbatim: 「6132 6166 同意」— the seat recommendation accepted): **Option A** — delete the five documented action props (`sonner action.onClick`, `context-menu onSelect`, `menubar onSelect`, `dropdown-menu onSelect`, `button-group onValueChange`) from the docs; where a real declared slot exists one level down (`MenuItem.onClick`), point the menu pages there instead. Every remaining line is true. The optional Option-B follow-up types card is NOT mandated — file one only if a real consumer for JSON-authorable actions on these components shows up (that filing would then meet #4453/#5329/#6107 precedents head-on, not sneak past them).

Downstream effect: this was the blocker on #5867's 71-file components group — that group unblocks when this card's deletion PR lands (note left on #5867).

State transition: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (this comment is the authoritative record if the label lags). Lane `domain:devx` (docs face), `documentation` stays. Size S–M mechanical (15 pages), sonnet-eligible.

## Zone 1 — The ruling (not re-litigable)

Maintainer, 2026-08-25, verbatim 「6132 6166 同意」 — the seat recommendation accepted. **Option A**:

> delete the five documented action props (`sonner action.onClick`, `context-menu onSelect`, `menubar onSelect`, `dropdown-menu onSelect`, `button-group onValueChange`) from the docs; where a real declared slot exists one level down (`MenuItem.onClick`), point the menu pages there instead. Every remaining line is true.

⛔ **The Option-B follow-up types card is NOT mandated.** File one only if a real consumer for JSON-authorable actions on these components shows up — and the ruling is explicit that such a filing *"would then meet #4453/#5329/#6107 precedents head-on, not sneak past them."* ⛔ Do not file it speculatively.

⭐ Note the shape of the two remedies, because it is the judgement in this card: a prop with **no declared slot anywhere** is deleted; a prop whose real slot lives **one level down** is redirected, not deleted. Getting one of these wrong in either direction produces a page that is still false — one that documents a prop that does not exist, or one that removes a capability the reader actually has.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify; the list is a lead, not a spec)

- The five props are **named**, but the ruling does not enumerate the **pages**. ⛔ Do not take a page list from the card, from this order, or from memory — **derive the sites from the tree** and report the population you found with the command that produced it. If your count differs from the card's "15 pages", yours governs and say which differed.
- ⚠️ **Establish `MenuItem.onClick` really is declared** before pointing three menu pages at it. The whole point of the ruling is that the redirect target exists; a redirect to a second undeclared prop would reproduce this card's defect while looking like the fix. Quote the declaration.
- Downstream: the ruling records that **#5867's 71-file components group unblocks when this card's deletion PR lands**, and a note was left on #5867. ⛔ Do not touch #5867 or widen into its scope — landing this is the whole contribution.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

Delete the prop rows outright where nothing declares them; for the menu family, replace the row with a sentence naming `MenuItem.onClick` and where it is declared, so the reader gets the working spelling rather than a silence. ⛔ My guess at the shape — if the pages read better another way, take that and say why.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. Docs pages sit in the doc-fence, doc-links and doc-snippet populations — follow each gate's own verdict rather than assuming which apply. `check-changeset-presence.mjs` decides whether a changeset is owed; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's own verdict line.

⚠️ Known trap on this repo's docs cards: `check:doc-snippets` exits non-zero with *"the packages it resolves against are not built"* / *"I could not run"* on an unbuilt tree. That is a **precondition, not your red** — declare it with evidence (fence counts base vs head) rather than reporting a green you did not get.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your branch — ⚠️ under `mode:subagent` your session ID will be identical to mine (objectstack#12220), so **the branch is what distinguishes your claim**, not the ID. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6132`.

## ACCEPT — PR #6345. ⛔ Deliberately NOT armed: a dissent window is open on #6346.

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### The landing hold, first, because it is the unusual part

The ruling redirects three menu pages at `MenuItem.onClick` **on the grounds that it is a real declared slot.** It is declared — and the dev verified that in three places before redirecting. But it measured the opposite fact underneath: ⛔ **no menu renderer reads it.** I re-derived that myself on `origin/main`:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `MenuItem.onClick` declared | ✅ `packages/types/src/overlay.ts:346` |
| the three renderers read `onClick` | ⛔ **zero hits** |
| what they actually read | undeclared `item.onSelect` — `context-menu.tsx:65`, `dropdown-menu.tsx:67`; `menubar.tsx` reads neither |

The probe is trustworthy because the same grep hits `onSelect` in those same files — a zero paired with a control, not a zero on its own.

⭐ **The dev did the right thing twice**: it executed the ruling **to the letter** (the ruling's stated test is "declared", which `onClick` passes, and the risk the ruling named — redirecting to a second *undeclared* prop — did not materialise), and it **filed the contrary fact instead of quietly widening into `packages/`**. That is exactly the behaviour this seat's rules ask for when an ordered action meets an opposing measurement.

So the rule for that situation applies: execute per the letter ✅, file the conflict as a decision ✅ (**#6346**, now `needs-user-decision`), and ⛔ **do not attach auto-merge — leave a dissent window**. PR #6345 stays **draft** and unarmed until the maintainer rules on #6346. It stays draft rather than merely unarmed on purpose: a ready PR can enter this repo's merge queue, and this seat put a governed-surface PR through that door by accident earlier today.

I also supplied the reading #6346's author said should be taken before ruling — whether any authored `onSelect` exists — because it was cheap and it was the thing blocking a recommendation. **Zero across `examples/`, `content/docs/` and `apps/`**, with a control confirming those directories do carry menu schemas. Analysis and a recommendation of option A are on #6346.

### ⭐ The population was 5 pages, not 15 — and the arithmetic closes

My order said to derive the sites and that the dev's count governs. It does, and the discrepancy is fully explained rather than merely asserted: the card's "15" was the whole **#6122** population (16 sites / 15 pages), of which **#6130 fixed 6** and **#6142 fixed 5**, leaving exactly these 5. Derived by command, and the same command returns nothing after the change. That is the difference between "I found fewer" and "here is where the others went".

### The delete-versus-redirect split, which was the judgement in this card

- **Deleted** where nothing declares the prop at any level: sonner's `action` (`SonnerSchema` declares no `action` — source, Zod mirror and renderer all agree) and button-group's `onValueChange`.
- **Redirected** where the slot is one level down: the three menu pages, with `MenuItem.onClick` verified in source, in the built `.d.ts` and in the Zod mirror before pointing anything at it — precisely the check my order demanded, since a redirect to a second undeclared prop would reproduce this card's defect while looking like the fix.
- ⭐ **Rejected a redirect I did not think to forbid**: `ButtonGroupButton.onClick` *is* declared, so it was an available target — and the dev declined it because a per-button click is not a group-level selection change, and the ruling scopes the redirect to the menu pages and names only `MenuItem.onClick`. Declining an easy, technically-available move because it would be *wrong* is the judgement this card needed.

### Gates

All green at `cb56e5ae1`, each quoted from the gate's own verdict line.

⭐ On the precondition trap I warned about: `check:doc-snippets` did first exit 2 (*"the snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built"*). The dev **neither reported it as a red nor declared a narrowing** — it ran the build the gate itself prescribes and re-ran, getting a **real** exit 0 with all three of the gate's own controls firing (sentinel → 1× TS2305, positive → 0, undeclared import → 1× TS2307), 267/267 blocks judged. That is strictly better than the declared narrowing I offered as acceptable.

Fence-count evidence base vs head: 10 plaintext markers before, 10 after, delta 0, and #5867's SHRINK-ONLY population unchanged at 80 files / 93 blocks — so nothing was converted into that card's scope.

### Out-of-scope findings — verified

**#6346** (the declared/inert mismatch — now the decision above) and **#6347** (four more undeclared props on the same two pages, plus a whole Selection Mode section documenting a capability the renderer does not implement). Both well-formed and unassigned. #6347 is the same defect class as this card at a wider radius and correctly left alone.

### What this does not block

⛔ #5867's 71-file components group unblocks when **this PR lands**, not when #6346 rules. If the maintainer takes option A on #6346, #6345 lands unchanged; under option B the three redirected pages need the same correction. Either way the hold is short and the reason is on the card.
